instruction:
Implement WP-SCP-022 Track 1 slice 020C.1 per WP-SCP-020 §4 row 020C.1. Six sub-criteria — close them all.

## Acceptance criteria

### (i) Waiver-aware Rego in the reusable workflow

- The reusable workflow `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` reads caller's `waivers.json` at the path given by `inputs.waivers-path` and passes it to conftest as `--data` (e.g., `conftest test --data waivers=$WAIVERS_PATH ...`).
- Each Rego rule (SCP-R-001/002/003) is updated to consume `data.waivers`. A `deny` only fires when there is no matching unexpired waiver (`expires_at > now` by `rule_id` OR `finding_id`).
- Add helper `scp_active_waiver_for(rule_id)` that looks up `data.waivers[_]` for a matching `rule_id` (or matching `finding_id` if a deny carries one) with `expires_at > now`. Each existing deny rule guards on `not scp_active_waiver_for(rule_id)`.
- When a deny would have fired but is suppressed by a waiver, emit an SCP-E006 observability record into the JSON summary `waivers_applied` list: `{rule_id, waiver_id_or_finding_id, expires_at}`.

### (ii) Canary fixtures

Three fixture branches/scenarios under `policies/testdata/conflict-gate/`:
- `hard-block/` — services.yml violates SCP-R-001; no waiver; deny fires.
- `waived-pass/` — same services.yml violation; matching waiver in waivers.json with future `expires_at`; deny suppressed; SCP-E006 emitted to `waivers_applied`.
- `rule-config-disabled/` — same violation; `.scp/rule-config.yaml` disables SCP-R-001 with `justification` + `expires_at`; deny suppressed; SCP-E006 emitted to `disabled_rules`.

### (iii) Conflict-gate (Python evaluator vs Rego rule disagreement)

- Python evaluators in `src/standards_control_plane/evaluators/` already emit findings. The conflict-gate is a NEW CI job `rego-vs-python-conflict` in `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` (alongside the main rego step) that runs BOTH engines on the same fixture set and asserts they agree.
- Disagreement = merge-blocked with `SCP-E005`. Plan rationale (not an auto-pass): "Python authoritative on conflict" is the eventual-resolution direction at CI time; runtime conduct = block until adjudicated.
- Unblock path: the amending D-NNN lands in a SEPARATE PR that updates `tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/<SCP-R-NNN>/<scenario>/expected-verdict.json` to match the ratified verdict. CI then green-lights when both engines' verdicts == expected. The blocked PR rebases onto main and re-runs.

### (iv) Conflict-gate mechanics

- `tests/conflict_gate/adapter.py` — normalises both engines' outputs to `{rule_id, file, verdict: allow|deny, reason: str}`. Reads Rego output (JSON from conftest), reads Python evaluator output (JSON from `src/standards_control_plane/audit.py` or equivalent), produces a unified record per rule per fixture.
- `tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/<SCP-R-NNN>/<scenario>/` containing `input.yml` (or `.json` for waiver/finding inputs) AND `expected-verdict.json`. Initial fixtures: at least one allow + one deny per rule.
- CI job `rego-vs-python-conflict` (in policy-check.yml or a separate workflow file `.github/workflows/conflict-gate.yml`): iterates fixtures, runs both engines through the adapter, asserts `rego.verdict == python.verdict == expected.verdict`. Any mismatch fails the job with SCP-E005.
- Pytest module `tests/conflict_gate/test_conflict_gate.py` runs the same adapter check locally (so devs can iterate).

### (v) Caller-side `.scp/rule-config.yaml` override

- New schema at `schemas/rule-config.schema.json` (draft 2020-12, `additionalProperties: false`):
  - `rules: { <SCP-R-NNN>: { disable: bool, justification: string, expires_at: date-time } }`.
- Rego rules check `data.rule_config[rule_id].disable` (default false). Disabled rules don't emit deny; emit `SCP-E006` to `disabled_rules` in JSON summary.
- Workflow reads `inputs.rule-config-path` (default `.scp/rule-config.yaml`) and passes to conftest as `--data rule_config=...`.
- A rule disabled in `rule-config.yaml` with `expires_at` in the past should emit a one-release warning annotation `::warning ::SCP-R-NNN rule-config disable expired YYYY-MM-DD; remove or extend the override`.

### (vi) Read-back (BS-4 closure)

- Every disabled rule (whether by waiver OR rule-config OR rule-config-deprecated) is emitted to:
  - JSON summary `disabled_rules` list with `{rule_id, reason, expires_at}`.
  - Commit-status text on `scp/policy-check`: "3 rules enabled, 1 disabled: SCP-R-002 until 2026-06-15 (rule-config override)". Use the workflow's commit-status post step or annotate via `gh api`.

## Existing files to extend (NOT replace)

- `policies/SCP-R-001.rego`, `policies/SCP-R-002.rego`, `policies/SCP-R-003.rego` — extend to consume `data.waivers` and `data.rule_config`.
- `policies/tests/scp_r_001_test.rego`, `_002_test.rego`, `_003_test.rego` — add cases for waiver-suppression + rule-config-disable + expired-waiver-no-suppression.
- `.github/workflows/policy-check.yml` — add waivers/rule-config data passthrough; add `rego-vs-python-conflict` job (or split into a separate workflow file).
- `schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json` — already has `disabled_rules` + `waivers_applied`; verify no schema change needed; tighten if necessary.

## New files

- `tests/conflict_gate/adapter.py`
- `tests/conflict_gate/test_conflict_gate.py`
- `tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/SCP-R-001/{allow,deny}/{input.yml,expected-verdict.json}` — at least one of each per rule.
- `tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/SCP-R-002/{allow,deny}/...`
- `tests/conflict_gate/fixtures/SCP-R-003/{allow,deny}/...`
- `policies/testdata/conflict-gate/{hard-block,waived-pass,rule-config-disabled}/...`
- `schemas/rule-config.schema.json`

## Constraints

- DO NOT modify pyproject.toml or tests/scp_mcp/ (Track 2 territory).
- DO NOT change DECISIONS / BACKLOG / STATUS. D-021 reservation respected.
- DO NOT introduce a 4th Rego rule (the v1.0.0 rule library is exactly 3).
- The conflict-gate is for EXISTING rules vs existing Python evaluators only. If a Python evaluator doesn't exist for a rule (e.g., SCP-R-003 vendoring marker), document the gap in `docs/integrations/conflict-gate.md` and skip the fixture for that rule (with a TODO referencing slice WP-SCP-022.1 or a follow-up).

## Self-test

The verify_commands assert structural file presence + critical invariants. opa test ≥90% per rule remains the workflow's enforcement gate.
verify_commands: python3 -c "import re,glob; assert len(glob.glob('policies/*.rego')) == 3, 'still exactly 3 rules in v1.0.0'"
python3 -c "import re; t=open('policies/SCP-R-001.rego').read(); assert 'data.waivers' in t or 'scp_active_waiver_for' in t, 'SCP-R-001 must consume data.waivers'"
python3 -c "import re; t=open('policies/SCP-R-002.rego').read(); assert 'data.waivers' in t or 'scp_active_waiver_for' in t, 'SCP-R-002 must consume data.waivers'"
python3 -c "import re; t=open('.github/workflows/policy-check.yml').read(); assert ('--data' in t and ('waivers' in t.lower())), 'workflow must pass waivers via --data'"

python3 -c "import yaml; d=yaml.safe_load(open('.github/workflows/policy-check.yml')); jobs=d.get('jobs',{}); names=set(jobs.keys()); assert 'rego-vs-python-conflict' in names or any('conflict' in k for k in names), 'rego-vs-python-conflict job missing'"
command -v opa >/dev/null 2>&1 && opa test policies/ -v 2>&1 | tail -10 || echo 'opa not local — CI runs it'
